corrections.original: Perceptrons was dedicated to Frank Rosenblatt (implying the 1969 book; Hook 1 'dedicated to the man it was read as burying').
corrections.fix: The documented dedication is the handwritten 'In memory of Frank Rosenblatt' that appears with the authors' handwritten alterations for the second printing (1972), after his July 1971 death. A 1969 first-printing dedication is unconfirmed (only Hecht-Nielsen's secondhand anecdote). Timeline and Hook 1 rewritten.

corrections.original: Key claim 1: connectedness cannot be computed without detectors that see 'a growing fraction of the' retina.
corrections.fix: Connectedness needs order growing at least as |R|^(1/2): an unbounded number of points per detector, not a growing fraction of the retina. Parity needs order |R| (some detector sees every point). Dossier body 5.3 was already correct.

corrections.original: Key claim 3 / 5.4: in 1969 nobody had a practical way to learn hidden-unit weights.
corrections.fix: Overstated. Amari 1967 (Saito's five-layer net with two modifiable layers) and Ivakhnenko's GMDH trained multi-layer systems, but they were little known in the US mainstream and were not a general method. Caveat added.

corrections.original: Richard Gregory, 'then at Edinburgh's Bionics Research Lab (later Bristol)' at the 1973 debate.
corrections.fix: Gregory left Edinburgh in 1970 to become Professor of Neuropsychology and director of the Brain and Perception Laboratory at Bristol, so he debated from Bristol.

corrections.original: McCarthy 'At the debate he argued that Lighthill's categories had "no place for what is or should be our main scientific activity"'.
corrections.fix: The quote is from McCarthy's written review of the Lighthill report, not from the televised debate. Re-attributed.

corrections.original: Michie: 'founder of Edinburgh's Department of Machine Intelligence and Perception'.
corrections.fix: Co-founder (1967) with Richard Gregory and Christopher Longuet-Higgins.

corrections.original: Olazaran shows the official history was built and institutionalised by symbolic-AI researchers 'who believed resources were being diverted from them'.
corrections.fix: Reworded to his abstract: the official history stemmed from the rise, institutionalisation and '(importantly) legitimation of the symbolic AI approach', including its funding allocation and authority structure.

corrections.original: Key claim 5: Papert admitted hostility 'partly over funding'.
corrections.fix: Verbatim confirmed. Added context from his next sentence: 'But most of the motivation for Perceptrons came from more fundamental concerns...'

corrections.original: Key claim 9: ALPAC found no prospect of useful MT after some $20 million of spending over ten years.
corrections.fix: The ALPAC wording is verbatim, including 'This is more than the government cost of translation for 1 year'. Hutchins (1996) argues US MT research funding 'may well have been nearer $12-13 million', and says ALPAC ended substantial US MT funding 'for some twenty years'. Say 'ALPAC put the figure at about $20 million'.

corrections.original: Key claim 15 / winter list: Werbos (1974) proposed backpropagation for multilayer nets.
corrections.fix: Schmidhuber calls the 1974 thesis only 'preliminary, NN-specific discussion' and dates the first NN-specific application of efficient BP to Werbos 1982. Werbos and Wikipedia credit 1974. Marked CONTESTED; keep 'invented several times'.

The Smithsonian says 'date made 1958'. Jensen and Dunning give assembly in June-December 1959, Nilsson a first public demo on 23 June 1960, and Wikipedia (Rosenblatt) hardware construction in 1960. Use 'around 1958-60'. The Smithsonian record (ID 1987.0819.01) also gives ONR and RADC funding, the 1967 transfer and 'Currently not on view'. The 400/512/8 counts are secondary.

corrections.original: Key claim 12: Lighthill debate date (9 May vs June vs 4 July filming / 30 Aug broadcast 1973).
corrections.fix: Still unresolved. The Edinburgh AIAI archive says 'June 1973'. Wikipedia's 9 May cites only a 2024 GitHub repo, and a note citing an SRI report gives 4 July / 30 August. No BBC Genome listing was found. Use '1973'.

corrections.original: Widrow: "So we stopped, basically stopped on neural nets" (via Olazaran 1991).
corrections.fix: Seen only via a secondary essay. Demoted to 'UNVERIFIED — do not use as a quote'; the paraphrase that he moved to adaptive antennas is kept.

corrections.original: LeCun 2016: the book 'had a hand in killing the first wave of neural nets, but it wasn't Papert's intention' (via QI).
corrections.fix: The Quote Investigator page does not contain it. It stays UNVERIFIED.

corrections.original: Q18: 'little of significance had changed since 1969' (1988 Prologue).
corrections.fix: Wording (had vs [has]) and location (Prologue p. vii per QI vs closing chapter per Wikipedia/Pollack) conflict. Marked UNVERIFIED as a verbatim quote until checked against the printed Expanded Edition.
